muse-wonder-1.0@max.answer:
The two platforms are not doing the same thing.

* **Left, 0-5s:** the people in the foreground barely change
position frame-to-frame. They are facing the track, standing
in a tight line at the platform edge — waiting to board.
That is the train we then see arrive and pass the camera.

* **Right, 0-5s:** almost nobody is standing facing the track
in a line. Individuals and small groups keep shifting position,
turning away from the edge and walking along / across the
platform toward the lit exits in the background. Their spacing
increases as they walk.

That motion is consistent with a crowd that arrived
*together, before the clip starts*, on the now-empty
right-hand track:

1. A train would have deposited them all along the length
of the platform, from different doors/cars — so they start
out spread in length.
2. They are now all doing the same thing at the same time —
walking away from the track toward the exit — which strings
a walking flow out across the width and length of the platform.

The left side, by contrast, is a stationary waiting crowd,
so it can remain packed in a tight boarding line.

criteria.justification: The candidate states the left-side crowd stands in a tight boarding line at the platform edge waiting to board the arriving train, while the right-side crowd, not boarding, spreads out.
